body:
### What happened

On 2026-11-07, in a hearsay-tools/cezarion worktree, a Pi worker (cezarion issue 2860) read `squeal status` twice, about 2 minutes apart, with no edits and no Squeal commands in between. The first read said a daemon was available. The second said no daemon was running. Nobody had run `squeal stop`. The worker started the daemon again by hand with `squeal start`. The host was loaded (4 parallel Cezar workers plus CI).

The exit reason was not recorded. One possible cause, not confirmed: in Pi sessions without the Squeal Pi extension, Squeal says no consumer is registered for the session (see the separate issue about that notice). The idle-exit rule from hearsay-tools/squeal#1 ("no session registered for N s after its last one ended") could then end the daemon while the agent is still working. Whether this worker's session had the extension was not recorded.

### What you expected

The daemon keeps running while the session that uses it is alive. If it does exit, the next `squeal status` gives the recorded exit reason ("stopped: no session registered for N s", "signal", an error), so the agent knows whether to restart it.

### Command and output

```text
squeal status   -> daemon available
(about 2 minutes, idle)
squeal status   -> no daemon is running
```

Exact output and JSON not recorded.

### Squeal version

not recorded at the time; current version is 0.1.412

### Squeal revision

not recorded

### Harness

Pi

### Model

not recorded

### Cost

One manual restart and the catch-up after it (minutes not recorded).

### Did a daemon restart clear it?

Yes, a restart cleared it

### Suggested fix

Always record why the daemon exited and print it in the next `squeal status`, including "no daemon is running" replies. If the cause is the no-session rule, treat a Pi session that calls the CLI (it has `PI_SESSION_ID`) as a live consumer even without the extension, or do not exit while CLI calls from that session keep arriving.

comments.body: The missing-consumer notice that the possible cause above refers to is hearsay-tools/squeal#164.

title: Worktree daemon exits while idle between two status reads, with no exit reason shown
